title: Fleet capacity sync — cross-region margins & migration risk notes (2026-03-18)
content:
Context:
This is the write-up from the weekly fleet capacity sync on 2026-03-18. Focus: cross-region headroom, an upcoming migration of non-latency-critical batch workloads off of us-west-2, and near-term risk mitigation for the H100 procurement delay. Attendees: Aisha, Diego, Linnea, Marcus, Samira + on-call SRE rotation (Rupen).

Summary (top-level):
- Current global peak GPU utilization (7d rolling) = 78% of provisioned capacity. Peak token throughput yesterday hit 1.9B tokens/day.
- us-west-2 remains the tightest region (85% peak), eu-west-1 at 74%, ap-northeast-1 at 62%.
- Planned migration: move ~120 A100 batch instances (non-interactive evals and nightly retrain) from us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 over two maintenance windows (Mar 25 and Apr 1).
- Procurement: H100 shipment delayed by ~3 weeks; contingency = temporary burst pool in partner colo + conservative prewarming of A100 nodes.

Notes from discussion:
1) Cross-region margins and triggers
   - Target headroom for each region at end of day: 20% for us-west-2, 25% for eu-west-1, 30% for ap-northeast-1. These reflect differing SLOs and customer mix (us-west-2 has more PLG spikes).
   - Trigger to pause migrations: if us-west-2 24h rolling drops below 15% free capacity for >4 hours OR error-rate on queued requests >0.5%.
   - Action: Diego to add automatic alert (pager) for the above trigger (INFRA-3498).

2) Migration plan (batch workloads)
   - Scope: ~120 A100 units supporting nightly evals, long-running QA sampling, and non-live retrain tasks.
   - Wave 1 (Mar 25): 60 units, wave 2 (Apr 1): 60 units. Each wave limited to 6 concurrent migrations to avoid network/IO spikes.
   - Pre-steps: update DNS routes for artifacts, warm container images in eu-west-1 registry, pre-pull caches. Marcus owns pre-warm checklist.
   - Rollback: if average job queue time increases >30% or failure rate >2%, rollback last wave.

3) H100 procurement delay mitigation
   - Temporary options discussed: (a) short-term partner colo burst capacity (costly), (b) selective quantization + dynamic batching to squeeze more tokens/sec from existing A100 fleet, (c) postpone non-critical experiments.
   - Decision: try (b) immediately + reserve up to 40 H100-equivalent slots with partner colo as fallback. Linnea to task quantization experiments; Samira to negotiate colo options and pricing.

4) Autoscale and prewarming tweaks
   - Observation: prewarming success rate in us-west-2 has dropped from 94% -> 88% when scaling >12 nodes at once. Suspected image-pull/registry throttling.
   - Interim fix: cap concurrent adds to 8 nodes per 30s for the next two weeks. Long-term: implement staggered pre-pull strategy in the orchestration layer.
   - Action: add a dashboard card in Console to show prewarm success by window (Diego).

5) Cost vs SLA tradeoffs for dedicated pools
   - Finance asked for short note on cost impact of pushing more customers into Dedicated pools vs hosted (to relieve us-west). A rough calc suggests shifting 2 medium enterprise customers (~250k tokens/day each) would free ~12% regional capacity at cost of increased reserved commit.
   - Action: Aisha to draft a one-pager for GTM to review by Mar 22.

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: unexpected PLG spike in us-west-2 during migration windows. Mitigation: hold back 10% capacity and pre-configure auto-fallback to eu-west-1 for stateless requests.
- Risk: quantization experiments introduce edge-case model regressions. Mitigation: run regression suite on canary traffic and block rollout if eval AUC drop >1.5%.
- Risk: registry throttles image pulls causing slow prewarming. Mitigation: mirror images to regional registries and add retry/backoff in runtime.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Diego: Pager alert for low headroom trigger (INFRA-3498) — due 2026-03-20.
- Marcus: Pre-warm & migration checklist + coordinate network IOPS limits — due 2026-03-22.
- Linnea: Run quantization perf/quality experiments and report results (A/B eval metrics) — initial results due 2026-03-24.
- Samira: Negotiate partner colo burst terms (max 40 slots) and publish cost scenarios — due 2026-03-23.
- Aisha: Draft GTM one-pager on Dedicated shift option — due 2026-03-22.

Standup snippets and quick logs (copied from meeting chat):
- "Prepull completed for batch images in eu-west-1; testing job runtime 3% slower, likely IO cold cache" — Marcus
- "We observed a small spike in queue depth at 04:22 UTC (us-west-2) — brief autoscaler lag" — Rupen (on-call)
- "Quantization trial config q2-128 reduced memory per model by ~22% on prelim run" — Linnea

Related tickets and references:
- INFRA-3421: Region capacity dashboard improvements (linked PR GH#1284).
- INFRA-3498: Migration pause/pager trigger (new).
- Runbook refs: playbooks/fallback-cross-region.md (internal).

Notes to follow-up in next sync (Mar 25):
- Verify migration wave 1 results and observed tail-latency impact (if any).
- Confirm partner colo readiness if H100 delay persists.
- Assess prewarm success metric after cap change and iterate.

Appendix (quick numbers snapshot):
- Provisioned GPUs by region: us-west-2: 1200 units (A100 equiv), eu-west-1: 840 units, ap-northeast-1: 420 units.
- 7d avg utilization by region: us-west-2 78%, eu-west-1 64%, ap-northeast-1 57%.
- Nightly batch job footprint (before migration): ~180 A100 units active between 02:00–06:00 UTC.

If anything here is unclear or you want raw logs/metrics dashboards, ping #infra-capacity or drop a note and I'll attach the queries/links.
